whyThisMatters: Real security moments offshore are fast, with limited time online — you don't get time to research if a link, a call, or a request is safe. This game trains your reflex for good habits, and helps you catch things that only sound safe.
rememberThis: This month's habit to carry forward: fast instinct is good, but some things only sound safe — a familiar-sounding voice, correct vessel details, an urgent deadline. When you are not sure, slow down and check before you trust the label.

discussionPrompts: Ask the group which bubble tricked them. Most people get at least one of the trick bubbles wrong on their first try.
Ask why a familiar-sounding voice on a call isn't proof of who's really calling.
Ask why taking longer to respond with limited signal is listed as a good habit here, not a delay to worry about.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: The most common mistake is tapping anything that sounds confident or familiar — a voice that sounds official, correct vessel details, an urgent deadline — without checking it through a channel you already trust. The trick bubbles are there to catch that habit.

bubbles.text: Pressed And Held Link Before Tapping
Hung Up And Called Back On Known Number
Verified Fund Request By Known Number
Checked Sender Domain On Rotation Email
Bought Gift Cards For Port Dues
Signed SEA Renewal Under Deadline Pressure
Ignored Domain Mismatch On Crew Portal

bubbles.note: Correct vessel or rotation details are a reasonable first check, but not proof of identity by themselves — this information isn't always private, and attackers use it specifically to sound credible.

bubbles.text: Slower To Respond With Limited Signal
bubbles.note: Taking longer to respond because of limited connectivity is a genuine safety net, not a delay to feel bad about — it gives you more time to notice something's wrong before you act.
A voice sounding familiar or confident is not proof of identity — the real check is calling back on a number you already have, not how the caller sounds.

bubbles.text: Called The Number In The Text
bubbles.note: A number given inside a suspicious text may connect straight to the attacker — only a number you already had counts.
